metadata.required_design_refinement: The doc's 'escalate exactly at the 3rd night' (consec == K) is fragile: if the classifier misses the Kth night (crash / rig down / send failure), the escalation is lost forever and D2's own guarantee ('no ever-passing benchmark goes unpaged past its 3rd consecutive failing night') silently breaks. IMPLEMENT INSTEAD: escalate when consec >= K AND no record inside the current consecutive-failure run already carries class == 'regression'. The JSONL schema already has the `class` field, so this needs no new state, stays replay-deterministic, still fires exactly once, and changes no verdict in the live replay. Flagged as a narrow strengthening of D2's escalation clause - controller may override before M3, but then the doc's 'never unpaged past night 3' claim must be softened.

Bootstrap is idempotent. ROLLBACK: revert the M1 commit; the JSONL is inert.

features.description: Implement D1.1-D1.5 + D5. Substrate only - the classification rule stays M1's, so an M2 failure can never be confused with an M3 failure. D1.1 unique key (date,bench,model,arm), --update-history = load -> drop tonight's keys -> append tonight's -> atomic write-back, duplicates resolve last-in-file-wins and compact. D1.2 window = records with date < tonight, tonight parsed from the --tonight dir name (nightly_eval_(\d{8})_rag_on), NEVER wall clock. D1.3 ownership-checked lock at ~/.ailang/state/nightly-eval-history.lock.d implemented VERBATIM to gpt5-6-sol's round-2 proposed_fix: atomic os.mkdir; dir stores PID + random ownership token; steal ONLY when os.kill(pid,0) confirms the holder dead; conservative recovery for unreadable/truncated metadata (possibly-live, steal only past a 10-min staleness threshold, log steal+reason at WARN, revert to PID-liveness if metadata becomes readable); verify token AFTER acquisition BEFORE the critical section; release only if the token still matches; 60s bounded wait then FAIL LOUD (non-zero exit). D1.4 write to <history>.tmp.<pid> in the same dir -> flush -> os.fsync -> os.replace; stray temps removed on the next locked update; unparseable lines skipped individually AND counted. D1.5 --bootstrap is an explicit one-off flag the nightly NEVER passes; absent history without it => D5 DEGRADED, never auto-seed. D5 HEALTH line into stdout + log + controlplane summary body. os.makedirs(dirname(history), exist_ok=True) for fresh machines.

M2.2 (TOP RISK - REAL SUBPROCESSES, NOT MOCKS): `-k Lock` passes test_held_lock_waiter_waits_bounded_then_exits_nonzero (asserts rc!=0 AND elapsed >= bound-epsilon AND <= bound+5s AND history byte-identical before/after), test_stale_but_alive_holder_is_not_stolen_from (lock mtime back-dated past 10 min while the holder PID is GENUINELY ALIVE => waiter must FAIL LOUDLY and must NOT steal), test_old_holder_resuming_after_replacement_detects_token_mismatch_and_does_not_write, test_ownership_checked_release_cannot_delete_another_process_lock, test_unreadable_lock_metadata_conservative_recovery. Any use of unittest.mock for os.kill or the holder process FAILS this criterion - a mocked stale-but-alive test passes against an mtime-only implementation, which is exactly what quorum round 2 rejected.

features.description: D2 window rule (W=5 nights-with-data, MIN_NIGHTS=2, MIN_TRIALS=4, all CLI-tunable via --window-nights/--min-nights/--min-trials/--escalate-after so tests can drive edges), D3 deletion of was_solid_in_prev, D4 routing in the shell. Labels REGRESSION / SUSPECTED-FLAKE / GAP / INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY per D2's table. ESCALATION USES THE REQUIRED REFINEMENT: consec >= K AND no record in the current consecutive-failure run already has class == 'regression' (NOT the doc's literal consec == K - see metadata.required_design_refinement); GAP windows excluded from escalation. Shell routing: REGRESSION -> per-bench --type bug (unchanged) + one Discord ping; SUSPECTED-FLAKE -> ONE aggregated --type note per night carrying per-bench `passes/trials over N nights` AND `failing X/3 toward escalation`; GAP -> aggregated --type note with the existing 'Gap-finder candidates' phrasing BYTE-IDENTICAL (eval-gap-finder is a text-contract consumer); INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY -> named in the summary body with shortfall + counter. Escalated REGRESSION bodies say 'escalated: 3rd consecutive all-fail night' plus the label escalated from.
acceptance_criteria: M3.1: `-k Rule` passes one test per row of D4's table on synthetic windows INCLUDING the boundaries: 2 nights/4 trials all-pass => REGRESSION; 2 nights/3 trials all-pass => INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY (MIN_TRIALS boundary); 1 night/4 trials all-pass => INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY (MIN_NIGHTS boundary)

M3.2 (THE V4 WEAKNESS IS DEAD, non-vacuously): test_single_trial_prior_night_cannot_certify_solid - one prior night with ONE passing trial + tonight all-fail => INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY, never REGRESSION. The SAME fixture must be asserted to yield REGRESSION under the OLD rule, so the test proves a behavior CHANGE rather than a tautology.

M3.3 (ESCALATION EXACTLY ONCE + MISSED-NIGHT ROBUSTNESS): `-k Escalat` - 5-night synthetic, mixed window then all-fail n1..n5 => EXACTLY ONE REGRESSION line across the 5 nights, at n3; n4/n5 emit SUSPECTED-FLAKE or GAP. PLUS the missed-night variant: skip the classifier on n3, run on n4 => escalation STILL fires at n4. This second test FAILS under the doc's literal consec == K, which is the point.
M3.4: test_never_passed_bench_does_not_escalate - window 0/6 over 3 nights + 3 consecutive all-fail => GAP, no escalation (real analogue: cli_args on 07-26)

M3.5 (D6 CONCESSION PINNED): test_new_benchmark_timeline - pass n1; all-fail n2 => INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY; n3 => SUSPECTED-FLAKE; n4 => escalated REGRESSION exactly once. MUST also assert the INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY line NAMES the benchmark and carries the counter - D5's visibility is what pays for the 48h delay, so it is tested, not promised.

M3.6 (THE ISSUE-CREATION GATE): `grep -nE -- '--type "?bug"?|--github' tools/launchd/nightly-eval.sh` - EVERY match lies inside the REGRESSION branch; ZERO matches in the SUSPECTED-FLAKE, GAP, INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY, or summary branches

M3.7 (SHELL ROUTING SMOKE): with a stub `ailang` on PATH that logs its argv, run the routing block against a fixture producing 1 REGRESSION + 2 SUSPECTED-FLAKE + 1 GAP + 1 INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY => captured argv shows EXACTLY 1x --type bug, 1x Discord send, EXACTLY ONE aggregated suspected-flake --type note, 1x GAP --type note, and a summary body containing both the HEALTH line and the `insufficient history:` line. A second --type bug FAILS M3.

M3.8: test_send_titles_embed_date - every generated title matches `.*\(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\)$`. The test DOCSTRING must record the R-F limitation: InboxMessageExistsByTitle (internal/messaging/inbox.go:563) skips archived/deleted rows, so exactly-once delivery holds only while nightly messages are not archived.
